conventions.convention: The continuum problem fixes one four-dimensional semiclassical solution, state and covariant renormalization prescription. It asserts no solution-existence theorem or empirical result.
Spacetime signature is (-,+,+,+); coordinates x⁰=ct and the affine generator parameter have length units. Cut entropy differences have SI units J K⁻¹.
Ordered cuts are graphs λ₁, λ₂ over the same nonempty compact boundaryless two-manifold, with λ₂(x)>λ₁(x) everywhere.

Regulator independence concerns finite limits of entropy differences across a specified nonempty admissible class containing at least two regulator constructions; separate finite limits of the absolute endpoint entropies are not required.
The Hadamard positive-frequency choice concerns the future-null covectors; the two base points may occur in either order along their common null geodesic.
The literature report is bounded and non-exhaustive through 22 October 2026. Failure of the cited results to establish the posed claim is not a theorem that no proof exists elsewhere.

alerts.finding: The Statement says, “Here x_N-r_N→L means that for every ε>0 there is an integer N₀ such that |x_N-r_N-L|<ε for all N≥N₀,” then concludes that r′_N=r_N-a satisfies x_N-r′_N→L+a. It defines convergence without assuming it. Taking x_N=N, r_N=0, L=0 and a=0 satisfies the explicitly stated real-sequence hypotheses but contradicts the conclusion. The Given and A1 do assume convergence, so the proof establishes the intended conditional result rather than the Statement as written.
